features.feature_value: Allow when constructive; remove when primarily attacking or making unverifiable claims
features.evidence_span: As long as the posts were not overly hostile and provided something constructive to say, I allowed them. If the posts seemed to only be attacking the other side or making claims that weren't verified, I removed them.
features.rationale: The participant explicitly states constructive/verified cues as the basis for keep/remove.

features.feature_value: Seeing both versions prompted applying the same harassment/abuse standard regardless of political alignment
features.evidence_span: Seeing both versions made me to apply the same standard to each side, even when one side was closer to my own views.
features.rationale: They describe the pair-viewing effect as forcing symmetric application of criteria.

features.feature_value: Assess each item independently using the same rules (e.g., harassment) rather than comparing viewpoints
features.evidence_span: intended approach is to assess each item against the same rules independently looking at things like whether there is harassment
features.rationale: They articulate a procedure of independent rule-based evaluation centered on harassment.

features.feature_value: Mentions that threats/harassment matter, but reflection text is partially garbled
features.rationale: Only a fragment about threats is interpretable; included cautiously due to limited context.

features.feature_value: Treat as protected unless there is a direct threat or crude language
features.evidence_span: If not a direct threat or crude language then it comes under free speech
features.rationale: They set explicit boundary conditions tied to free-speech framing.

features.feature_value: Remove content that makes hateful remarks about division and discrimination
features.evidence_span: remove those that made hateful remarks about division and discrimination
features.rationale: The participant directly names the content type that triggers removal.

features.feature_value: Alternate perspective framing affected judgment (e.g., naming a person vs generic reference)
features.evidence_span: conservative post was generic but the liberal post mentioned someone by name
features.rationale: They cite specific framing differences as influencing their evaluation.

features.feature_value: Keep opinions; remove if nonsense/lies with harmful effects
features.evidence_span: If it was something that was mainly an opinion, I thought it should stay... If it appeared to be nonsense... and I thought it was actually harmful, I thought it should be removed... But if they are flat out lies, I think they should not remain.
features.rationale: They provide a rule differentiating opinions from unverified harmful falsehoods.
